 By Chicago Tribune PUBLISHED: October 23, 2026 at 5:00 AM CDT | UPDATED: October 25, 2026 at 3:35 PM CDT Illinois voters will decide Nov. 3 who will replace retiring U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin and whether Gov. JB Pritzker wins a third term . Chicagoans will elect 20 members to the city’s first fully elected school board and a citywide school board president .
 Those races top a midterm ballot that also includes an open race for state comptroller, legislative contests that could affect Democrats’ supermajorities in the state House and Senate and several historic congressional races in the Chicago area.
 Early voting is already underway, and polls will be open from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day.
 Here’s what to know about the races on your ballot, along with where to vote , how to register and what to bring.
 Illinois voter guide to the 2026 midterm elections in November 
 Sign up for our Politics newsletter “The Spin” for the latest election news 
 Senate
 U.S. Senate Republican nominee Don Tracy, left, and Democrat nominee Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, right, sit onstage with anchor Brandis Friedman, center, during a live televised U.S. Senate candidate forum at the WTTW-Ch. 11 studios on Oct. 20, 2026, in Chicago. (Armando L. Sanchez/Chicago Tribune) 
 The race for the Senate seat held by veteran Democrat Dick Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January, is highlighted by Democrat Juliana Stratton, 61, who is the first Black person to serve as Illinois lieutenant governor, and Don Tracy, 76, a Springfield attorney and former state Republican Party chair.
 American Center Party candidate Whitfield Harrington is also on the ballot.

 Governor
 Gov. JB Pritzker, left, and Republican nominee challenger Darren Bailey prepare for their gubernatorial debate at WTTW-Ch. 11 on Oct. 13, 2026, in Chicago. (Armando L. Sanchez/Chicago Tribune) 
 Darren Bailey, a downstate farmer, is seeking to reverse his loss to Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker four years ago.
 Bailey, whose two runs for governor have been endorsed by Donald Trump , has tried to escape the president’s unpopularity in populous northeastern Illinois by focusing his campaign on local issues such as crime and property taxes while avoiding his evangelical Christian conservative opposition to abortion and LGBTQ+ rights.
 Independent candidate Collin Corbett, a former Republican political operative, is also on the ballot.

 Board of Education
 Anchor Brandis Friedman, back to camera, briefs candidates for the Chicago Board of Education president Jessica Biggs, from left, Hilario Dominguez and Victor Henderson before a forum at WTTW-Ch. 11 in Chicago on Sept. 15, 2026. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune) 
 Chicago voters will cast ballots for the city’s first fully elected school board, selecting 21 members to steer the future of Chicago Public Schools.
 There are 38 candidates across 20 district-level races, along with three candidates running for the citywide board president seat. A handful of board hopefuls also are running write-in campaigns. Voters will cast two votes: A candidate to represent their district, and another for board president. Here’s what else to know .
 Voting in Chicago’s school board elections? Find your district with our lookup tool.

 Statewide races and General Assembly
 Democratic state Rep. Margaret Croke of Chicago, left, and Republican Bryan Drew, a lawyer from southern Illinois, are vying for the state comptroller office in this November's election. (Chicago Tribune) 
 Illinois Democrats have held every statewide constitutional office since early 2019, and a sweep would extend that lock on state government to 12 years. The Illinois comptroller is the only statewide office without an incumbent running, and two candidates from opposite ends of the state are vying to fill the spot.
 In the Illinois General Assembly, all 118 House seats and 39 of the 59 Illinois Senate seats are on the ballot. While there’s no sign the legislature is flipping red, the Illinois GOP hopes recent scandals involving Democratic state lawmakers will breathe new life into the party’s efforts to gain more relevance.
 Illinois comptroller race: Margaret Croke and Bryan Drew vie for open seat as Democrats seek statewide sweep 
 Illinois Democrats on defense over scandals in races for state legislature 
 Congress
 Cook County commissioner Donna Miller, center, the Democratic nominee for Illinois' 2nd Congressional District, mingles outside St. Sabina Church in Chicago at a peace march Oct. 2, 2026. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune) 
 Of Illinois’ 17 congressional districts, five seats are open in the Chicago area and downstate, from the 2nd District, which covers the city’s Far South Side through the south suburbs to Danville, to the 9th District, which runs from the Far North Side to parts of McHenry County. The one constant is that Democrats hold all five seats now and the party’s nominees are favorites to win them on Nov. 3.
 2nd District: Democrat Donna Miller aims to succeed Robin Kelly — and stay for years 
 4th District: Chuy García’s handpicked successor Patty García defends path to Congress

 Cook County
 Pat Hynes takes a congratulatory phone call from Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle after defeating Fritz Kaegi for the Democratic nomination for Cook County Assessor on primary election night at Salerno's Pizzeria & Sports Bar, March 17, 2026, in Hodgkins. (John J. Kim/Chicago Tribune) 
 Races in Cook County are also on the ballot as voters will select a new Cook County assessor. They’ll also decide if Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle deserves another term. Democrats are heavily favored in all the races.
 Cook County assessor favorite Patrick Hynes vows ‘stability,’ detente with appeals board 
 Where to vote
 Residents vote early at Martin Luther King Community Service Center in Chicago on Oct. 20, 2026. (Antonio Perez/Chicago Tribune) 
 To find your local polling location, type your address and ZIP code here .
 In Chicago, early voting began Oct. 1 at two locations: Chicago Board of Elections (sixth floor, board offices) , 69 W. Washington St., and the new Loop Supersite , 137 S. State St. Early voting expands to polling places in each ward Oct. 19. Here’s a list of where you can vote early in each ward . Search  here to find out what ward you live in .
 If you live outside Chicago, select a jurisdiction to find where you can vote before Election Day.
 To register in person, you must bring two forms of identification, one of which must list your current address. Here is a list of acceptable forms of ID for Chicago voters and suburban voters . If you are registered to vote and your address is correct, you do not need to bring your ID — though it’s not a bad idea to bring it in case your signature doesn’t match the one on file.
